judge.reason: The answer rejects the P85 claim by stating that a PERT mean is not a percentile and that summing means doesn't give one. It gives labeled, uncalibrated scenarios (3/9/12.5/36 days), notes that dependence widens the spread rather than assuming independence, refuses to give a confidence level, and offers Monte Carlo only as a clearly conditional, unrun option. It also separates the work forecast from the commitment with an explicit end buffer, and treats calibration from actuals (task 1 duration, re-forecast points) as follow-up, though it never explicitly says to gather comparable history from past work.
